failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Agents used an over-specific label or a nearby retrieval detail instead of following the clue's requested answer level or explicit referent.

rejected_edits.content:
## Work-title clues
- For terse clues featuring a work title, do not assume the answer is the title itself or a principal person associated with it. Infer the intended relation from the clue and context: it may point to a source or work being retold, or to a creator, performer, character, or other clearly identified relation. Use an explicit contextual association when the clue makes that relation clear; if no intended relation can be established, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.
rejected_edits.target:
## Bare work-title prompts
- If a prompt consists only of a work title and year, do not answer with its generic type (such as “film”). Look for a principal person explicitly and centrally associated with that work in the context, such as its director, author, or creator, and answer with that person only when the association is clear. If the context offers no clear intended relation, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.

rejected_edits.content: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity. When the context supplies a concise answer label, use it rather than adding merely descriptive expansions. When a category is already specified, normally give the distinguishing value rather than restating the category; however, retain a category-like word when it is integral to the context-supported canonical proper name or title.
rejected_edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity. When the context supplies a concise answer label, use that form rather than expanding it into a fuller name, title, or role description merely because the expansion is also correct. When a category is already specified in the question, provide the distinguishing value rather than repeating the category.

rejected_edits.content: - For completion or compound clues, normally provide only the missing component; when alternatives share a component, give that component rather than one full alternative. For partial-name prompts, give only the requested unknown name part. However, when the prompt asks you to identify an established proper name, title, or other named entity—not merely fill a blank—use its context-supported canonical full form, including a clue-supplied component when needed to identify the referent. Otherwise, omit components already stated unless they are needed for unambiguous identification.
rejected_edits.target: - For completion or compound clues, identify the missing shared component that makes the alternatives fit; do not repeat a clue-supplied component or return one full compound. For partial-name prompts, give only the requested unknown name part. Omit components already stated in the question unless they are needed for unambiguous identification.
